item.title: Wikimedia's home page has no h1.
item.description:
Preloaded HSTS, a content security policy starting at default-src 'self', and a sitemap per language. But the home page has no h1, and several About pages have two.
The lesson for every team: One h1 per page, naming what the page is. Screen-reader users often jump to it first.

item.title: FAO's HTML is fast. Visitors still wait.
item.description:
The home page HTML arrives in about 0.2 s, behind preloaded HSTS and a content security policy. But real Chrome visitors wait 4.7 s at the 75th percentile for the largest content to appear.
The lesson for every team: Find your Largest Contentful Paint element, load it early, give it a size, and never lazy-load it.

item.title: Creative Commons moves to https with 302.
item.description:
A sitemap index, pages that name their language, and robots meta that allows large previews. But http:// reaches https through a temporary 302, and no page analyzed sends Strict-Transport-Security.
The lesson for every team: Use a 301 from http to https, then add Strict-Transport-Security so browsers skip http next time.
One automated analysis of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict. How the review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=runs-100-2026-11&utm_content=creativecommons
#WebSecurity #HTTPS #HSTS #QA #QAlab

item.title: The EFF's pages send no HSTS.
item.description:
A content security policy in report-only mode, nosniff, framing limited to its origin, and a sitemap. But no page analyzed sends Strict-Transport-Security, so browsers don't upgrade a first http visit.
The lesson for every team: Add Strict-Transport-Security with a long max-age. It tells browsers to use https before the request leaves.
One automated analysis of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict. How the review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=runs-100-2026-11&utm_content=eff

Every internal link that was opened answered, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds.
Lesson: Keep body text at a 4.5:1 contrast ratio or more against its background.

item.title: artisan-emmanuel.fr: 69. The gap: form labels.
item.description:
Every internal link that was opened answered, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But 21 form controls have no label.
The lesson for every team: Give every input a visible label tied to it with for and id. Screen readers announce it, and the tap target grows.

item.title: baltbet.ru: 34. The gap: button names.
item.description:
Every internal link that was opened answered, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But buttons must have discernible text.
What to change: Give every button text or an aria-label, so a screen reader can announce it.

item.title: opinautos.com: 52. The gap: framing.
item.description:
Every internal link that was opened answered, and model-training crawlers are blocked by choice. But other sites can frame the page.
What to change: Send frame-ancestors 'self' in the CSP, or X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, so other sites cannot frame your pages.
